trust_decision.summary: Frames from the CAN bus are trusted to fit the device's state. Two checks are missing: the LSS handlers look up 0x1018 identity subindexes and never check for a NULL entry (src/co_lss.c), and the SDO server accepts a segment request whatever the current job type is, so it reuses a stale data pointer from a different or finished transfer (src/co_sdo_server.c).

landing_point.why: The summary says 'CANopen NULL pointer dereference'. The only unchecked co_entry_find result passed straight into co_od_get_value is in the LSS identity getter. The SDO server sites are a job-state confusion, not a NULL dereference.

fix_sites.entry_point: CAN id 0x7E5 -> co_handle_rx (src/co_main.c:86-89) -> co_lss_rx switch-selective 0x40-0x43 and identify-remote 0x46-0x4B -> co_lss_match -> co_lss_identity_get
co_lss_init called from NMT init (src/co_nmt.c:98); fix adds CC_ASSERTs that 0x1018 and subindexes 1-4 exist
CAN id 0x600+node -> co_handle_rx (src/co_main.c:77-80) -> co_sdo_rx ccs=3 upload segment (src/co_sdo_server.c:560-561)
CAN id 0x600+node -> co_sdo_rx ccs=0 download segment (src/co_sdo_server.c:566-567)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/co_sdo_server.c:427-459 (a second, unrelated module and mechanism, SDO job-type confusion with a write to the stale job->sdo.data, shipped in the same fix as an LSS NULL dereference: fix.diff:135-174)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory is a NULL pointer dereference (CWE-476) and its obvious site is LSS. The SDO server segment handlers dereference no NULL, run a toggle check and only touch job state, so a solver can argue they are a different, protocol-conformance issue.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate segmented upload and download continuation must still work when job->type matches. LSS must still answer a missing identity subindex with UINT32_MAX (the fix test expects a device whose subindex 1 is missing to still be selected by 0xFFFFFFFF), and inquire NODE_ID (0x5E) must keep returning net->node with no identity lookup. Dropping the LSS frame or rejecting every segment would break these.

O6_input_shapes: LSS: switch-selective commands 0x40-0x43 reaching co_lss_identity_get with a missing subindex
LSS: identify-remote commands 0x46-0x4B reaching the same getter
LSS: inquire-identity commands 0x5A-0x5D with a missing subindex (fix routes them through the getter)
LSS: 0x1018 object or subindexes 1-4 missing at init (CC_ASSERT only)
SDO server: upload segment request while the job is a download, none (after expedited, abort or 0xFF structure query)
SDO server: download segment request while the job is an upload (stale data pointer from co_od_get_ptr of a read-only object) or none

O7_producer.where: src/co_lss.c:556 caches net->lss.identity = co_obj_find(net, 0x1018) once at init; for SDO, the stale job->sdo.data and remain values are produced by the init handlers at src/co_sdo_server.c:187-192 and src/co_sdo_server.c:357-363

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The SDO client response handlers never check job->type. Upload responses reaching a WRITE job memcpy peer data into the caller's const source buffer, and download responses reaching a READ job copy the read buffer onto the bus.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: This is the master/client side, which talks to a slave it addressed itself. The advisory and fix concern the SDO server, and co_sdo_tx already checks the node id (src/co_sdo_client.c:234).
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different file (src/co_sdo_client.c), same src/ directory as the server fix

O8_uncovered_routes.route: If 0x1018 is absent, net->lss.identity is NULL. co_entry_find dereferences obj before the fix's new NULL-entry check, so only the init CC_ASSERT guards it, and that may compile out.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Identity object 0x1018 is mandatory in CiA 301, so a missing object is a device misconfiguration, not attacker input.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: src/co_od.c, one file from the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An SDO block upload/download handler (CiA 301 ccs 5/6) that reuses job_sdo_server and continues a transfer without checking job->type
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Block transfer is a standard SDO service missing from this server; a maintainer adding it would copy the segment handlers' pattern.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An LSS identify-non-configured or inquire variant that reads 0x1018 directly through co_entry_find/co_od_get_value instead of the getter
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: inquire_identity at the pinned commit already duplicated the getter inline (src/co_lss.c:356-357).

O9_family: NULL pointer dereference plus protocol state confusion (stale pointer write that bypasses read-only access), memory safety (native)

O10_build.toolchain: CMake + googletest + rtlabs osal + cmake-tools submodule; at the pinned tree there is no CMakeLists.txt, no options.h template, no osal and no cmake/ directory (submodule declared at .gitmodules:1-3)
O10_build.project_tests: test/test_lss.cpp, test/test_sdo_server.cpp, test/test_sdo_client.cpp (gtest with mocked os_channel_send / co_obj_find, test/mocks.h)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a NULL check on entry inside co_lss_inquire_identity only, or bail out of the LSS command, and leave the SDO segment handlers and client untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: The SDO client calls co_sdo_abort, which resets net->job_sdo_server.type (src/co_sdo_server.c:61, src/co_sdo_client.c:91-96), so client errors cancel the server transfer; the client also sends aborts on 0x600+net->node and 0x580+net->node rather than to the peer.
The sample slave diff (fix.diff:46-61) is a demo loop change, not a security fix.
unverified: Definition of CC_ASSERT (osal cc.h is absent from the tree), so whether the init asserts survive release builds is unknown.
Repo size in MB was not measured; about 50 source files, clearly under 5 MB.
Buildability: the pinned tree lacks CMakeLists.txt, osal and the cmake-tools submodule; a build would need these reconstructed from upstream rtlabs repositories.
Whether the SDO client routes are still present upstream (no latest release given).
